NH-2026-SB425.aiSummary: The bill would lower the age limit for the adjutant general and deputy adjutant general from 65 to 64. It would also set new term rules for those jobs and change how the commandant of the New Hampshire veterans’ home is chosen. The commandant would be nominated by the home’s board of managers and appointed by the governor and council for a 4-year term.

NH-2026-HB1755.aiSummary: The bill would require 340B covered entities in New Hampshire to file yearly reports on drug costs, savings use, charity care, patient collections, and other program data with the health and human services department and the attorney general. The health and human services department would then send a combined report to lawmakers and post it online, and the director of charitable trusts would review the data for compliance with charity rules. It would also set fines for late reports and take effect on January 1, 2027.

NH-2026-HB772.aiSummary: Would set up a new funding system for public schools called foundation opportunity budgets and state grants. It would also redefine what counts as an adequate education and set statewide learning standards from kindergarten through grade 12. The bill would affect school districts, local school boards, and state education officials by changing how public education is planned and funded.

NH-2026-HB1579.aiSummary: The bill would create a committee to study ways to raise state revenue for more education aid. It would look at new revenue sources and changes to current ones, and study how they could affect the state, businesses, and people of different income levels and ages. The committee would also look at whether some options could help fund education and lower property taxes.

NH-2026-HB648.aiSummary: The bill would require several kinds of health insurance in New Hampshire to cover glucose monitors and related supplies for people with diabetes. It would apply to individual and group health plans, health service corporations, and health maintenance organizations. The bill would also cap insulin costs at $30 for a 30-day supply and would bar deductibles, prior approval, and certain referral rules for this coverage.

NH-2026-HB1670.aiSummary: The bill would create crimes for organized retail theft and for leading a group that commits it. It would let thefts be added together over 180 days, allow cases to be brought in any county where part of the activity happened, and require courts to order forfeiture of property tied to the crime. It would take effect 60 days after passage.

NH-2026-HB604.aiSummary: The bill would set up a loan forgiveness program for lower-income homeowners who build or renovate accessory dwelling units, or ADUs, which are small extra homes on the same property. The New Hampshire Housing Finance Authority would run the program, and loans could be forgiven if the ADU stays affordable and other program rules are met. Homeowners who break the rules would have to repay the loan. It would take effect July 1, 2025.

NH-2026-HB1450.aiSummary: The bill would change the rules for shared rental housing, where people have private sleeping areas but share spaces like a kitchen or bathroom. It would require a written statement saying the property is a shared facility and would treat a lessee, not just an owner, as able to control one. The law would take effect 60 days after passage.

NH-2026-HB1692.aiSummary: The bill would change the youth advisory council’s size, membership, duties, and day-to-day rules. It would add an application process for youth members, set dates for applications and reports, and make most council records public while keeping application materials private. It would also require a website page for the council and take effect when passed.
